title: Open Graph Checker: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Open Graph Checker: Preview a page's Open Graph and Twitter Card tags as they appear when shared. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example…
content:
The [Open Graph Checker](/open-graph-checker) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Preview a page's Open Graph and Twitter Card tags as they appear when shared. Enter your page URL and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

See how a page will look when it is shared: fetch the URL and preview its Open Graph and Twitter Card tags — the title, description and image that Facebook, X, LinkedIn and messaging apps show in the share card. Missing tags mean a plain link instead of a preview, and a missing or wrong image is the most common share-preview failure. The fetch runs from this site's server with the usual safety limits, and nothing is stored.

## How to use the Open Graph Checker

Start by typing or pasting your page URL. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste the full URL of the page to preview, starting with https://.
2. Run the check and read the share preview.
3. Add any missing tags — usually og:image — and re-check.

## How it works

The [Open Graph Checker](/open-graph-checker) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Checking a page with og:title, og:description and a 1200×630 og:image shows a full preview card. Without an og:image, the preview shows text only. Try the same figures in the [Open Graph Checker](/open-graph-checker) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [Open Graph Checker](/open-graph-checker) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## Which tags make a share card

og:title and og:description set the card's text, og:image sets the picture, og:type (usually “website” or “article”) and og:url complete it. Twitter Card tags (twitter:card, twitter:title, twitter:description, twitter:image) do the same for X — if they are missing, X falls back to the Open Graph tags. An og:image of 1200×630 pixels gives a full-size card; without one, the share shows a small thumbnail or none at all.

## Why previews go wrong

The usual failures are a missing og:image, an image that is too small or blocked, and tags that differ from the page's title and description. Social platforms also cache previews — after fixing tags, a page can still show the old card until the platform re-fetches it (Facebook's Sharing Debugger and X's Card Validator force a refresh). This tool shows the tags as they are now, so you can see what the platforms will see next time.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Use a 1200×630 image for a full-size share card.
- Check that the preview text matches the page — not a generic site slogan.
- After fixing tags, refresh the platform's cache (Sharing Debugger / Card Validator).

## Frequently asked questions

### What are Open Graph tags?

Meta tags (og:title, og:description, og:image) that tell Facebook, LinkedIn and messaging apps what title, text and image to show when a page is shared. Try it with your own numbers in the [Open Graph Checker](/open-graph-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Why does my shared link show no image?

Usually a missing og:image, an image that is too small, or one the platform cannot load. Add a 1200×630 og:image and re-check. Try it with your own numbers in the [Open Graph Checker](/open-graph-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is the difference between Open Graph and Twitter Cards?

Open Graph is the general standard; Twitter Card tags are X's version. If Twitter tags are missing, X falls back to the Open Graph tags. Try it with your own numbers in the [Open Graph Checker](/open-graph-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### I fixed the tags but the share still looks old — why?

Social platforms cache previews. Use Facebook's Sharing Debugger or X's Card Validator to force a fresh fetch after fixing tags. Try it with your own numbers in the [Open Graph Checker](/open-graph-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
